pages.title: New oral anticoagulants versus warfarin in atrial fibrillation

sections.heading: Pooled efficacy and safety across four trials

claims.text: In a prespecified meta-analysis of 71,683 participants in the RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trials, new oral anticoagulants significantly reduced stroke or systemic embolic events by 19% compared with warfarin (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.73-0.91; p<0.0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0.49, 0.38-0.64; p<0.0001).

evidence.quote: We did a prespecified meta-analysis of all 71,683 participants included in the RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, and ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 trials. The main outcomes were stroke and systemic embolic events, ischaemic stroke, haemorrhagic stroke, all-cause mortality, myocardial infarction, major bleeding, intracranial haemorrhage, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

New oral anticoagulants significantly reduced stroke or systemic embolic events by 19% compared with warfarin (RR 0·81, 95% CI 0·73-0·91; p<0·0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38-0·64; p<0·0001).

claims.text: New oral anticoagulants also significantly reduced all-cause mortality (0.90, 0.85-0.95; p=0.0003) and intracranial haemorrhage (0.48, 0.39-0.59; p<0.0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1.25, 1.01-1.55; p=0.04).

evidence.quote: New oral anticoagulants also significantly reduced all-cause mortality (0·90, 0·85-0·95; p=0·0003) and intracranial haemorrhage (0·48, 0·39-0·59; p<0·0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1·25, 1·01-1·55; p=0·04).

claims.text: There was a greater relative reduction in major bleeding with new oral anticoagulants when the centre-based time in therapeutic range was less than 66% than when it was 66% or more (0.69, 0.59-0.81 vs 0.93, 0.76-1.13; p for interaction 0.022).

evidence.quote: We noted no heterogeneity for stroke or systemic embolic events in important subgroups, but there was a greater relative reduction in major bleeding with new oral anticoagulants when the centre-based time in therapeutic range was less than 66% than when it was 66% or more (0·69, 0·59-0·81 vs 0·93, 0·76-1·13; p for interaction 0·022).

claims.text: Low-dose new oral anticoagulant regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (1.03, 0.84-1.27; p=0.74), and a more favourable bleeding profile (0.65, 0.43-1.00; p=0.05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1.28, 1.02-1.60; p=0.045).

lint.note: Trial conclusions differ by agent and dose: dabigatran 110 mg was similar to warfarin for stroke/systemic embolism with less major hemorrhage, dabigatran 150 mg was superior for stroke/systemic embolism with similar major hemorrhage, apixaban was superior for stroke/systemic embolism with less bleeding, and edoxaban high dose was noninferior with less bleeding while low dose was noninferior with more ischemic strokes in the meta-analysis. Each conclusion is kept with its own trial and dose.

In ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 the low-dose edoxaban regimen was noninferior to warfarin for stroke or systemic embolism, whereas the meta-analysis reports that low-dose new oral anticoagulant regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events but significantly more ischaemic strokes; the difference in outcome definition and pooling is kept with both sources.

The global ROCKET AF trial used rivaroxaban 20 mg daily in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, while J-ROCKET AF used a Japan-specific 15 mg once-daily dose in Japanese patients; the dose and population difference is kept with each trial.
No document gives a head-to-head comparison of the new oral anticoagulants against each other; all comparisons are against warfarin or placebo.
